_readme: Occasions the channel should notice. Two kinds.
`recurring` entries fall on the same date every year (MM-DD) and need no maintenance.
`dates` entries move with the lunar calendar and must be filled in each year. They are
listed with their dates left empty on purpose: these dates were NOT guessed, because a
wrong festival date on a customer channel is far worse than no post at all. Fill them
from a panchangam or a printed calendar, as { "2026": "2026-11-08" }. An entry with no
date for the current year is simply skipped — nothing breaks, the post is just an
`note` is written for whoever generates the post. Say what the day is, what people
actually cook, and what to be careful about. It is read by the model, not by customers.
`aliases` are the names this festival goes by in Google's national holiday feed, which npm run calendar:fill reads. Regional festivals (Bathukamma, Bonalu) are not in that feed and stay manual.

occasions.name: New Year's Day
occasions.note: Everyone marks it, nobody is excluded by it. People are full of resolutions that will not survive February — so the useful post is the small habit that actually lasts, not the grand plan. Do not mention weight or 'starting fresh' in a way that implies last year was a failure.

occasions.name: Sankranti
occasions.note: The biggest festival of the year in Andhra and Telangana, and a harvest festival — three days, families travel home, houses get muggulu at the door. Food is ariselu, sakinalu, pongali, chakkara pongali, payasam, and a lot of jaggery and til. Sweets are the whole point; do not tell anyone to eat fewer of them. A good post is about enjoying them without the afternoon slump — eat with the meal rather than instead of it, and drink water.

occasions.name: Republic Day
occasions.note: A national day, not a religious one. Flag hoisting at schools, an early start, and often a dry day. Keep it light and unifying. Do not use it as a hook for anything patriotic-sounding about food.

occasions.name: Independence Day
occasions.note: As Republic Day: national, secular, early morning, school events. Children are up and out early, so a breakfast angle fits naturally.

occasions.name: Teachers' Day
occasions.note: Small and warm. School-age children are involved. A light post at most; it does not need a food angle forced onto it.

occasions.name: Gandhi Jayanti
occasions.note: A national holiday and a dry day. Widely observed as a vegetarian day — do not suggest non-vegetarian food on this date. Simple, plain food suits the day.

occasions.name: Children's Day
occasions.note: About children. The natural post is what children will actually eat — lunchboxes, after-school hunger, letting them help cook. Never about children's weight, and never anything a parent could read as criticism.

occasions.name: Christmas
occasions.note: Greet it warmly and briefly. A minority of readers celebrate it and the rest have colleagues and neighbours who do, so write it as 'to those celebrating' rather than assuming. Cake and sweets are the food; treat them the way the Sunday post treats a cheat meal.

occasions.name: Ugadi
occasions.note: Telugu New Year, and the most local festival on this list after Sankranti. Ugadi pachadi is the whole idea — six tastes together, sweet and bitter and sour, standing for a year that will hold all of them. That is a genuinely good food post and needs no stretching. Raw mango, neem flower, jaggery, tamarind.

occasions.name: Maha Shivaratri
occasions.note: Many readers fast all day and stay awake at night. Never tell anyone to break a fast, never call fasting unhealthy, and give no medical opinion on it. If food is mentioned at all, it is what people actually eat when they break it — fruit, milk, sabudana — and the useful advice is to break it gently rather than with a heavy meal.

occasions.name: Holi
occasions.note: Less central here than in the north but widely enjoyed. Colours, water, and being outside in the heat. Hydration is the honest angle. Food is gujiya, thandai, sweets.

occasions.name: Sri Rama Navami
occasions.note: Panakam and vada pappu are handed out at temples and homes — jaggery, cardamom, dry ginger, soaked moong dal. Both are seasonal cooling foods in peak summer, which makes the food angle write itself.

occasions.name: Ramzan (Ramadan)
occasions.note: A month, not a day, so fill both the first and last dates if you use it. Muslim readers fast from before dawn to sunset. Never tell anyone to break or keep a fast and give no medical opinion on fasting. If the post touches it at all, it is practical and respectful: what makes sehri last until evening, and breaking the fast gently — dates, fruit, water — rather than heavily. Do not schedule a post that centres on daytime eating as though everyone is eating.

occasions.name: Eid al-Fitr (Ramzan Eid)
occasions.note: A celebration at the end of the fasting month. Greet it warmly, as 'to those celebrating'. Sheer khurma, biryani, sweets. Treat the food the way the Sunday post treats a cheat meal — it is a feast day and nobody needs advice about eating less at it.

occasions.name: Bakrid (Eid al-Adha)
occasions.note: Greet warmly and briefly. Mutton is the food of the day. Keep any suggestion inside the channel's non-vegetarian list, and do not comment on the observance itself.

occasions.name: Bonalu
occasions.note: Telangana, in the monsoon month of Ashada. Cooked rice with milk and jaggery carried to the temple. Local and worth marking for Telangana readers.

occasions.name: Vinayaka Chavithi
occasions.note: Big here, and lasts days. Undrallu, kudumulu, modak, laddu. Households are cooking steamed rice-flour sweets in quantity. Steamed rather than fried is the natural, non-preachy observation.

occasions.name: Bathukamma
occasions.note: Telangana, nine days, flowers and women's gatherings, ending with Saddula Bathukamma. The food is the five saddulu — curd rice, tamarind rice, lemon rice, coconut rice, sesame rice. A genuinely good food post.

occasions.name: Dasara (Vijayadashami)
occasions.note: Ten days of Navratri and then Dasara. Many readers eat only vegetarian food through Navratri, so do not suggest non-vegetarian food during it. Fasting is common — the fasting rules above apply.

occasions.name: Deepavali
occasions.note: The biggest sweets-and-fried-snacks week of the year. Boxes of sweets arrive from everywhere and sit on the table for a fortnight. Do not tell anyone to eat fewer sweets at Deepavali — nobody will listen and it makes the channel a nag. The useful post is about the days after: what to eat when the house is full of sweets, and keeping one proper meal a day.

occasions.name: Karthika Pournami
occasions.note: The month of Karthika Masam. Many readers eat only vegetarian food for the whole month and some fast on Mondays — so avoid non-vegetarian suggestions across it if you can, not only on the day.

occasions.name: Guru Nanak Jayanti
occasions.note: A small number of readers, but greeting it costs nothing and excluding it is noticed. Short and warm.

occasions.name: Good Friday
occasions.note: A day of fasting and abstinence for observant Christians. Sombre rather than celebratory — do not greet it the way you would greet a festival. If in doubt, post an ordinary post that day.
